subject: Post-call recap: SignalCore discovery — latency & throughput constraints + topology asks
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Asha Menon <asha.menon@signalcore.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@signalcore.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Feb 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: SignalCore discovery — latency & throughput constraints + topology asks

Hi Asha / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we stay aligned before the technical deep-dive: the goal here is to validate feasibility of powering SignalCore's realtime recommendation endpoint with predictable latency while keeping unit cost within your target band.

Key pain points you shared:
- P95 latency target: <= 120ms for the 1k-2k token prompts (primary constraint).
- Tail behavior: occasional spikes at 99th that caused user-visible delays.
- Peak throughput: ~180–220 concurrent inference requests (regional peak), diurnal shape with a 30% evening spike.
- Model constraints: prefer an open Llama-based 13B / 34B variant, willing to try quantized variants if quality holds.
- Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and tenant isolation required for pilot.

Agreed success criteria for pilot:
1) Sustained P95 <= 130ms at 200 req/s for 48h test window (production-like traffic shape).
2) No more than 2x baseline cost vs initial estimate once quantization and batching are applied.
3) Visible fallback plan (multi-variant routing) that keeps errors < 0.2% under capacity constraints.

Initial topology options we discussed (we'll formalize in the deep-dive):
- Dedicated GPU pool (preferred) with autoscaling and burst policy to cover evening spikes.
- Multi-variant routing: quantized 13B for cost; 34B (higher-latency) as fallback for quality-sensitive routes.
- KV / prefix caching for repeated context to reduce token work.

Immediate asks from our side (please provide before the deep-dive):
- Anonymized production request sample (CSV): fields: timestamp, avg_tokens_in, avg_tokens_out, endpoint, p95/p99 observed latency. (We list a suggested template in the attached latency_poc_sheet.xlsx)
- Clarify expected context length distribution (avg/95th).
- Any internal SSO / VPC constraints for an on-prem or VPC connector pilot.

Attachments: latency_poc_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet with template), placeholder for metrics export.

Next steps:
- Please confirm two windows for a 60–90min technical deep-dive next week (Rishi + Karthik + infra folks). I have open slots Tue/Wed 8–11am PT or Thu 1–4pm PT (link to calendar below).
- Fill out the attached template and drop the CSV to the Drive link.

Thanks — I'll coordinate invites once I get preferred windows.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Lauren — thanks for the clear summary. Quick clarifications and commitments from our side:

- We'll anonymize and share a 48-72h sample export with the columns you requested (expect to deliver by Wed EOD).
- Context length: median ~450 tokens, 95th ~1,600 tokens. Average output tokens ~40.
- Peak shapes: we saw 200rps sustained for ~30min windows; 8pm PT is a regular nightly spike for our West coast users.
- Model preference: start with 13B quantized variant; we will run E2E QA comparing output quality vs 34B if latency constraints can't be met.

One more ask: we currently have an internal high-latency endpoint that we can point you to for benchmark runs (can give temporary credentials). We'll include that in the CSV export.

Thanks team — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive:

1) Pilot topology I recommend we validate in the first run:
   - Dedicated GPU pool (4x A10 / 8x A10 depending on memory profile) behind Redwood dedicated routing.
   - Autoscaling based on moving-window QPS and queue latency; burst capacity configured to 1.5x baseline for evening spike coverage.
   - Multi-variant routing: quant-13B (primary) at lower cost, 34B (fallback) with traffic-splitting by route and SLA.

2) Performance levers we'll test during the 48h run:
   - Continuous batching: tune max_batch_size and max_latency_ms to hit P95 targets without over-saturating GPU memory.
   - KV/prefix caching for repeat prefixes (expected 12–18% token reduction for your workload).
   - Model quantization profile: 4-bit dynamic vs 8-bit fallback; we'll A/B quality with your QA prompts.

3) Data we need (matches Lauren's asks):
   - Per-endpoint QPS over 7 days (5m granularity)
   - Sample request payloads (anonymized) and tokenization stats
   - Any model-specific constraints (max_context, tokenization differences)

4) Security/compliance note: for SOC 2 evidence and separation, we'll need the contact for your infosec reviewer and an outline of any contractual data residency needs.

I can own the performance test design and the runbook for the 48h window. If you can share the CSV and a test credential, we'll schedule a non-prod run before the pilot.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
